title: Start reading a board
summary: Choose Computer screen, keep the whole board visible, then use Scan now. Auto suggest follows later moves.
questions: How do I start using BoardLens?
How do I show it a chessboard?
steps: Board → Read from → Computer screen.
Choose Display to read. All displays checks every connected monitor.
Keep all 64 squares visible and move BoardLens away from the target.
Press Scan now. Enable Auto suggest to follow moves.
details: Screen reading and engine thinking are separate. Use the separate connections for supported 3D boards.

title: The board is not being found
summary: Scan now starts a fresh read. Check the selected display, whether the board is covered, and whether a target lock is keeping an old board selected.
questions: Why can’t it see my chessboard?
The scan keeps searching and never finds my game
It stopped detecting after I changed apps
steps: Check Board → Display to read.
If Keep this board selected is on, return to that board or turn it off.
Keep the whole board visible. Scan now clears old recognition and releases a locked suggestion.
For supported themes or 3D views, try the Browser connection or Local 3D chess connection.
details: Pixel recognition supports known 2D artwork. Arbitrary 3D screenshots are not supported. OS screen-recording permission is needed for pixels.

title: Scan now and Auto suggest
summary: Scan now refreshes from the visible board immediately. Auto suggest keeps reading and requesting new analysis after moves.
questions: What is the difference between Scan now and Auto suggest?
How do I force a refresh?
steps: Use Scan now after switching games or when a position is stale.
Use Auto suggest for continuous tracking.
Keep this board selected stays active during a rescan; turn it off if you want a different target.
details: Scan now cancels obsolete reads and analysis. It never clicks a move in the real game.

title: Stop scanning and thinking
summary: STOP cancels live reads and engine searches, then hides screen overlays.
questions: How do I stop everything?
How do I pause the bot?
steps: Press STOP, Escape while the main window is active, or the configured Stop shortcut.
Use Auto suggest or Scan now to start live reading again.
details: Previous/Next pauses live tracking for history navigation.

title: Choose where the position comes from
summary: Practice is a local board you can edit. Computer screen follows another visible app. Screenshot reads a file you choose.
questions: What does Read from mean?
How do I analyze an image?
steps: Practice board: click pieces or load a FEN.
Computer screen: choose a display and scan.
Screenshot: choose Open screenshot, then a complete supported 2D board image.
details: Orientation controls which color appears at the bottom. Side to move corrects uncertain live turn detection.

title: Screen scanning or an optional connection?
summary: Standard 2D boards use screen scanning with Use browser extension off. Turning it on prefers connected browser boards; if no extension board is available, screen scanning continues. Local 3D chess is a separate option.
questions: Do I need the browser reader for local 3D chess?
Why are there two connections?
Can I use it without the extension?
steps: Use Computer screen for supported flat 2D boards.
Use Browser connection for supported Chess.com/Lichess positions and themes.
Use Local 3D chess for the built-in macOS Chess app.
details: A connection being off does not disable the other reading methods. Local 3D chess currently supports macOS Chess.app, rather than every 3D chess program.

title: Connect the browser
summary: Turn on Use browser extension to prefer it for 2D and supported 3D/theme boards on Chess.com and Lichess. Turn it off for normal screen scanning. Optional connections contains status and pairing controls.
questions: How do I connect Chess.com or Lichess?
Where is the browser pairing key?
steps: Board → Computer screen → Use browser extension.
Connection setup explains loading BoardLens 2/BrowserReader in Chrome or Edge.
Copy pairing key. Paste it into the extension popup and choose Connect.
Reload the chess tab and keep it visible.
details: The loopback service uses port 8788. Positions stay on this computer. The extension cannot play moves or change settings. Browser data can preserve more metadata than a screenshot.

title: Repair a disconnected browser
summary: The extension retries temporary interruptions. Its status distinguishes a missing key, an offline desktop, and an invalid pairing.
questions: Why does the browser disconnect?
It says key repair or context invalidated
The browser reader needs to reconnect
steps: Keep Use browser extension enabled in BoardLens.
If the key is rejected, copy the current key into the extension and reconnect.
After an extension update, reload the extension once and reload the chess tab.
Keep the chess tab visible; switching away normally releases its feed.
details: The browser pairing key survives desktop restarts. This differs from the phone code, which changes when its companion restarts.

title: Read Local 3D chess
summary: Local 3D chess reads the built-in macOS Chess app through Accessibility, independently of the browser connection.
questions: How do I use local 3D chess?
Why does the local connection need permission?
steps: On Mac, enable Read local 3D chess in Optional connections.
Grant BoardLens/Python Accessibility in System Settings → Privacy & Security.
Open the local Chess board and press Scan now.
details: Its status says Ready until its supported app is active, then Connected after a board is read. Other local 3D programs and arbitrary camera/artwork screenshots are not covered.

title: Keep one board selected
summary: Keep this board selected prevents other apps or boards from replacing your target. A covered or missing target pauses instead of switching.
questions: How do I stop it switching to another board?
Why does it keep showing my old board?
How do I unlock the target?
steps: Read a live board first. If several are present, choose the target in Board.
Turn on Keep this board selected.
Turn it off to follow other apps again.
details: Pixel targets remain at their captured area; unlock and rescan after moving/resizing them. Direct readers keep their source identity. Overlays hide when another app covers a locked target.

title: Analyze several boards
summary: Up to three boards have independent positions, engine sessions and recommendations.
questions: Can I analyze three boards at once?
How do I get back to one board?
steps: Show complete boards on your selected displays.
Use Scan now to discover them.
Use Boards to see their cards together, or Focus for the primary board.
details: Cards disappear when boards are no longer detected. New-board discovery also runs periodically. Each engine session adds its own thread and memory usage.

title: Your color and whose turn it is
summary: Only my color treats the color at the bottom as yours. Side to move is a separate control for uncertain live positions.
questions: How does it know which color I am?
It is showing the opponent’s moves
How do I change whose turn it is?
steps: Enable Only my color for suggestions on your turns only.
Board → Detect bottom color normally handles orientation automatically.
On a static live position, set Side to move to White or Black if needed.
details: Only my color forces automatic orientation. A screenshot/DOM read may lack complete castling, en passant or turn history. A full FEN on Practice preserves exact metadata.

title: Choose an engine
summary: Analysis engine selects the recommendation provider manually. The Engine library manages optional downloads.
questions: How do I choose another engine?
Where are Maia and the tiny bots?
steps: Open Engine → Engine library.
Choose the engines to download; large neural models are optional.
After installation, select the engine in Analysis engine.
details: Selecting an unavailable engine gives a setup message. BoardLens never downloads or switches engines silently. Installed engines are skipped in download batches.

title: Maia human-style predictions
summary: Maia-2 and Maia-3 predict human choices at a target rating. They do not use Stockfish search depth or time limits.
questions: Why are depth and time disabled for Maia?
What does Maya rating mean?
How do I download Maia without reinstalling?
steps: Download the chosen Maia entry in Engine library.
Select it manually and set Human target rating.
Request suggestions normally.
details: No separate reinstall button is needed. Its scores are human-game outcome estimates, not objective Stockfish evaluations or guaranteed playing Elo. Maia-2 uses Rapid rating bins; models need their optional runtime and weights.

title: Stockfish skill and Elo
summary: Full strength searches without a strength limit. Skill level and Elo rating deliberately change its selected recommendation.
questions: How do I make Stockfish weaker?
What does skill 10 mean?
steps: Choose Stockfish.
Set Stockfish strength to Full strength, Skill level or Elo rating.
Adjust the active skill/Elo control.
details: The supported Elo range depends on the installed Stockfish build. #1 is its strength-limited choice; alternatives can have better objective scores. The evaluation bar uses the strongest searched evaluation.

title: Think time, depth and adaptive limits
summary: Time sets seconds of thinking. Depth sets a search depth. Time + depth stops at the first limit. Adaptive stays under both caps.
questions: How long should the engine think?
What is time versus depth?
Why did a five second search finish early?
steps: Time: use seconds only.
Depth: use a fixed depth; elapsed time can vary widely.
Time + depth: whichever limit is reached first stops the search.
Adaptive: reduce time/depth based on move count, checks and captures.
details: Stop cancels thinking. Maia uses a model pass; Tiny bots support their own timed move choice, not full Stockfish depth analysis.

title: Make suggestions arrive sooner
summary: Screen refresh targets 75 ms independently of engine think time. Show moves while thinking can display intermediate results while the full search continues.
questions: Why do the arrows take so long?
Can it refresh faster without changing engine time?
The board updates slowly
steps: Use Show moves while thinking to see an early result.
For a faster completed search, reduce Think time yourself or choose a shallower supported limit.
Use fewer suggested moves and suitable threads per board to reduce work.
details: The 75 ms screen interval is fixed, not a guaranteed move-to-arrow delay. Capture permission, recognition, engine startup and drawing add latency. Direct connections bypass artwork recognition.

title: Threads and memory
summary: CPU threads and hash memory apply per analyzed board. More is not always faster on a busy computer.
questions: What do threads and hash mean?
Why is my computer using lots of CPU?
steps: Set CPU threads to the number you want per engine session.
Set Hash memory for the engine’s position cache.
Remember that three boards and engine comparison start separate searches.
details: Maia and Tiny bots do not expose all of these Stockfish controls.

title: Playing styles
summary: Balanced keeps the native recommendation. Other supported styles rerank close candidates using visible tactical and positional facts.
questions: What does aggressive or defensive do?
How do I get human-like moves?
steps: Choose an engine with style support.
Select Balanced, Aggressive, Defensive, Human-like or Maximum strength.
Use Maia when you want a model trained on human decisions.
details: These styles do not rewrite an engine’s internal evaluation. Tiny bots keep their coded behavior. Maximum strength removes Stockfish’s skill/Elo limit.

title: Tiny bots, Flounder and custom UCI
summary: Tiny bots choose one move without detailed evaluation or alternatives. Flounder samples Stockfish-derived choices; custom UCI uses an executable you supply.
questions: Why can’t this bot show five moves?
Why is the evaluation blank?
steps: Read the selected engine’s capability note.
For Tiny bots use one suggestion; download its shared .NET runtime through Engine library.
For Custom UCI choose its executable in Engine files.
details: Reference Elo is not guaranteed at your search budget. Flounder’s target rating is approximate. Custom multiple recommendations require MultiPV support.

title: Compare engines side by side
summary: Comparison runs two or three chosen engines on the same position without changing your main engine.
questions: How do I compare Maia with Stockfish?
Can I compare three engines?
steps: Expand Compare engines in Engine.
Choose engines A and B; choose C or None.
Press Compare engines.
details: Each comparison keeps its own results and errors. Human estimates and objective engine evaluations are labelled separately.

title: Save and load a named preset
summary: Presets store engine and display choices. Quick analysis and Deep analysis are built in.
questions: How do I save my engine setup?
What do presets save?
steps: Configure the engine and arrows.
Use Save preset and enter a name.
Choose a saved preset to load it; Manage renames, updates or removes custom entries.
details: Presets include limits, strength, style, move count, arrow filters and threats. They exclude screen refresh, display choice, connection keys and readers. Missing engines must be installed first.

title: Settings save automatically
summary: Your preferences save after a short editing pause and when you close BoardLens. Installed engines live outside the app folder.
questions: Will it remember my settings after closing?
My settings keep resetting
How do I save my choices?
steps: Finish editing a value and wait briefly.
Save now writes immediately.
Apply keybinds activates shortcut edits.
Keep the application-data folder when updating the application.
details: Phone changes sync to desktop and then save. Invalid unfinished shortcut text is not saved. Your selected analysis preset is preserved.

title: Arrow colors and alternatives
summary: Gold is #1, blue is #2, and later colors are more alternatives. Cyan is the opponent’s best reply after #1.
questions: Why does the blue arrow look different?
What does the cyan arrow mean?
Are both arrows moves I should play now?
steps: Choose Suggested moves in Engine.
Use Arrows → Moves to draw and rank filters to control visibility.
Opponent reply shows a continuation after the best move, not a second move for the current turn.
details: Only my color, Lock move and color/rank filters can intentionally hide arrows. Rank labels identify alternatives. Dashed reply is optional; solid is the default.

title: Stop suggestions flickering
summary: Steady arrows smooths intermediate replacements while analysis continues. Lock move keeps the first displayed move until the position changes.
questions: Why do the recommended moves keep changing?
How do I keep one arrow while the engine calculates?
steps: Use Steady arrows to keep calculating with fewer visible changes.
Use Lock move when you want one fixed recommendation for the current position.
Changing the board or pressing Scan now releases that locked suggestion.
details: Evaluation still updates. The first hint and completed engine result are immediate; provisional replacements need to remain consistent briefly.

title: Screen arrows let clicks through
summary: Screen overlays are passive. You should still be able to move pieces in the target app with arrows visible.
questions: Do the arrows block my mouse?
How do I turn screen arrows off?
steps: Toggle Arrows in the top bar, Screen arrows in the Arrows tab, or the arrow shortcut.
This changes screen overlays without stopping monitoring or engine thinking.
details: The mirrored board and phone can still show their own hints. Covered or unconfirmed target boards may hide screen overlays temporarily.

title: Read the evaluation bar
summary: Positive values favor White; negative values favor Black. M means the engine found a forced mate. The bar is not a winning percentage.
questions: Why does it say White is winning?
Is +2 a 100 percent chance to win?
What does M3 mean?
steps: Read the signed score next to the board. +1.00 is roughly a pawn-sized engine advantage for White.
A neutral dash means there is no supplied evaluation yet.
Use Full analysis for the complete explanation and variations.
details: Strength-limited suggestions and Maia predictions are labelled. Maia scores describe human-game outcomes; Tiny bots do not supply an evaluation.

title: Threat highlights
summary: Red rings mark possible material loss in legal capture exchanges. Purple rings mark mate-in-one targets for the side to move.
questions: What are the red and purple circles?
How do I show attacked squares?
steps: Arrows → Threats → Threat highlights.
Show attacked squares adds dots for the opponent of the bottom color.
Show mate-in-one targets enables purple targets.
details: These bounded capture checks are estimates. They do not prove every tactic or assess all sacrifices. Hover the mirrored board for explanations.

title: Review previous live positions
summary: Previous and Next browse observed positions while live reading pauses. Resume live returns to the current target.
questions: Does Undo change the real game?
How do I go back through moves?
steps: Use Previous/Next below the mirrored board.
Resume live returns to current play.
On Practice, Undo removes a local move.
details: History never undoes moves in another app. Resume live to continue following your current board.

title: Use the local Practice board
summary: Practice is an editable board inside BoardLens. It never controls the external game.
questions: How do I play moves without changing my real board?
What does Play best do?
steps: Board → Read from → Practice board.
Click a piece, then its destination. Click promotion chooses a queen.
Suggest requests analysis; Play best makes exactly one local move.
New game resets the local board; Undo takes back a local move.
details: Practice moves stay inside BoardLens. External boards receive suggestions only.

title: Load and copy a FEN position
summary: FEN describes one exact chess position, including whose turn it is.
questions: What is position FEN?
How do I load an exact position?
steps: Load FEN on Practice for exact turn, castling and en passant metadata.
Copy FEN shares the current position.
details: Invalid FEN is rejected. Pixel reads cannot recover every historical right from artwork alone.

title: Keyboard shortcuts
summary: Keys configures shortcuts for suggestions, scanning, overlays, history, Stop and one local Practice move.
questions: How do I change keybinds?
My keyboard shortcuts do not work
steps: Enter pynput notation such as <ctrl>+<alt>+s or <cmd>+<shift>+b.
Use Apply keybinds to validate and activate all entries.
Global shortcuts work outside BoardLens when OS permissions allow them; otherwise use focused-window shortcuts.
details: Default Ctrl+Alt keys: S Suggest, A Auto suggest, B Scan, H Arrows, X Stop, Left/Right History, L Resume, M one Practice move. Escape stops while the main window is active.

title: Compact, full analysis and staying on top
summary: Compact prioritizes the board. Expanded keeps settings beside it. Full analysis gives the workspace to the explanation.
questions: Where did my settings go in compact view?
How do I make the analysis text bigger?
steps: Use Compact/Expand in the top bar.
In Compact, Settings opens the same tabs in a separate window.
Full analysis expands the text; Text − / + changes its size.
Stay on top keeps the desktop window above other windows.
details: Compact resizing retains the current display and position when possible. Settings content wraps and scrolls vertically.

title: Pair a phone or tablet
summary: Enable the desktop companion, use the same network, then enter its computer address and six-digit code on your phone.
questions: How do I connect my Android phone?
Can the GUI be on my iPad?
steps: Desktop → Phone → Enable phone companion.
Open the Android companion or the shown address in a phone/tablet browser.
Enter the six-digit code.
Start with BoardLens enables the companion automatically on desktop startup.
details: The computer must stay awake and running; minimizing its GUI is fine. The connection port can be changed before enabling the companion. iOS native source still needs your signing setup.

title: Phone settings sync to desktop
summary: Phone edits are sent after a short typing pause, reflected in desktop controls and saved there.
questions: Why don’t my phone settings change the desktop?
Do I have to press Apply every time?
steps: Wait for Synced with your computer.
Apply now retries an interrupted edit.
Paths sync after editing finishes; keyboard shortcuts have their own Apply button.
details: If a desktop modal dialog is open, close it before remote edits. Disabled settings reflect the selected engine’s capabilities.

title: Reconnect the phone
summary: After the companion restarts, pair again with its new code. Keep the desktop running on the same reachable network.
questions: My phone cannot reach the computer
Why did the pairing code change?
steps: Check the address in the desktop Phone tab.
Keep the companion enabled and the computer awake.
Check Wi-Fi and local firewall access.
Enter the current six-digit code.
details: The phone code differs from the persistent browser-extension key. A local address is not reachable from arbitrary internet connections.

title: Copy buttons
summary: Copy buttons show Copied to clipboard when text is available. An empty value reports that there is nothing to copy.
questions: Did it copy the pairing key?
Where did my copied text go?
steps: Use a Copy button for a position, configuration or pairing value.
Paste the text into the app or field where you need it.
details: The clipboard belongs to the device where you tapped Copy. The phone reports a browser clipboard restriction if copying fails.

title: Update BoardLens from GitHub
summary: Check for updates manually in Board → App. Android has its own app-update button.
questions: How do I update BoardLens?
Where is the update button?
Can I update the APK?
steps: Desktop: Board → App → Check for updates.
If a newer desktop build is available, choose Download and restart.
Android: Check for app updates on the connection screen, or Controls → Update Android app.
Confirm an Android installation in the system installer; grant installation access only if you want that update.
details: Downloads come from Nick-PY0/BoardLens releases and are checksum-verified. Desktop keeps a rollback copy and preserves settings, engines and runtime. Android also checks the package identity, version and signing certificate. A desktop restart requires pairing the companion again.

title: Choose the evaluation engine separately
summary: Engine → Evaluation bar selects who scores the position. It is independent of the move engine.
details: Use Stockfish for the bar while Maia or another engine recommends moves. Evaluation think time and depth cap apply only to the evaluator. Maia uses a human rating rather than search limits; its value head is an estimate, not Stockfish centipawns.
steps: Choose a recommendation engine.
Choose an Evaluation engine, time, and depth cap.
The bar shows its provider and updates when that separate job finishes.
questions: Can I use Maia moves with a Stockfish evaluation bar?
Why is the evaluation different from the selected engine?

title: Predict the next two moves
summary: Predict opponent and my next move adds a reply and your following move for every engine.
details: The first recommendation is shown as soon as the provider returns it. Single-move models then analyze the next two positions with the same engine. These are predictions, not guaranteed play. Each extra search uses the selected search budget. Turning this off saves work. Non-streaming models must finish their first inference before there is a result.
steps: Enable Predict opponent and my next move in Engine.
Enable Show moves while thinking to show the first result before the continuation finishes.
Steady arrows keeps the display calm while calculation continues.
questions: Can Maia predict what I play after the opponent?
Why do predictions take longer than one move?

title: Automatic app updates
summary: Board → App → Automatic updates checks and downloads stable desktop releases quietly. A verified update installs at the next launch.
details: Your current game is never interrupted. Turn this off to keep manual update control. Archives are checksum checked and staged with rollback. Android checks automatically, then opens the public release; Android controls installation. APKs withheld from a release cannot be installed by the updater.
steps: Enable Automatic updates in Board → App.
Keep using BoardLens; any download stays in the background.
Close and reopen when convenient to install.
questions: Can it update automatically?
Will an update interrupt my game?

title: Maia, Tiny bots and prediction controls
summary: Maia 2 and Maia 3 predict one move per model pass. Prediction length controls how many moves BoardLens calculates in a line.
questions: Can I change Maia depth or thinking time?
What does predict opponent and my next move mean?
What are early suggestions?
How do Tiny bot limits work?
steps: Choose your recommendation engine manually. The evaluation bar has a separate engine.
Enable Predict opponent and my next move. Prediction length 3 means your move, the predicted reply, then your response. Each ply is one move by one side.
Reply time budget limits additional predictions after the first move. BoardLens does not wait for the budget to expire. A Maia pass in progress may complete after it.
Show moves while thinking displays partial results as soon as available. Turn it off to show only the finished result. Steady arrows keeps arrows stable while the engine calculates.
details: Stockfish and compatible search engines accept a depth and/or think time. Time + depth stops at whichever limit comes first. Adaptive varies work within both caps. Maia 2 and all Maia 3 sizes use single-pass human move prediction, so depth and longer think time do not improve their first move. Their target rating, prediction length and reply budget are useful controls. Tiny bots use their coded search/style and an adjustable bot clock budget; most do not expose native depth or alternative moves. Predicted replies are possibilities, not promises. A different real opponent move starts a fresh analysis.

title: Manual settings and presets
summary: Manual means you are using the controls individually, rather than a saved preset. All settings save automatically.
questions: What is Custom settings?
What is Manual?
Do my engine settings save?
steps: Choose an engine and adjust its supported controls.
Save preset stores that combination under a name.
Quick analysis and Deep analysis are ready-made Stockfish configurations.
details: Analysis limit chooses when search finishes. Time uses seconds; Depth uses plies of search; Time + depth stops at the first limit. Adaptive searches within both caps. Manual itself does not start analysis; Suggest or Auto suggest does.
